title: Random Bubble Art
body:
Goal: fill the screen with 30 bubbles at random places, random sizes and random colors. Every time you press Run, you get a brand-new picture!

  1. Open starter.py and press Run (F5). 30 bubbles... all in the same place, so it looks like one bubble.
  2. Follow the # TODOs inside the loop and use the random module:
    • x = random.randint(-350, 350) (a random whole number from -350 to 350)
    • y = random.randint(-250, 250)
    • size = random.randint(10, 50)
    • color = random.choice(PALETTE) (picks one color from the list)
  3. Press Run a few times. Is it different every time?

Done looks like: colorful bubbles all over the screen, different every run.

Extra: add a second command, def star(x, y, size, color):, and mix stars and bubbles. Or try a dark background: turtle.bgcolor("#000000").

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look inside the for loop in starter.py. Every round uses the same four values, so all 30 bubbles land in the same spot. Find the # TODO notes next to x, y, size and color.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: The random module is already imported at the top. It can pick a random whole number between two limits. It can also pick one item from a list. Use those so each round gets new values.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: For a number, use random.randint(____, ____) with the smallest and biggest allowed values. For a color, use random.choice(____) with the list name inside. Put one of these on each of the four lines inside the loop, in place of the fixed values.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Random Bubble Art
# random makes surprises: a new picture every time you press Run.

import random
import turtle

# The color-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette
PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.speed(0)
t.hideturtle()


# bubble(x, y, size, color) draws a filled circle with its middle at x, y
def bubble(x, y, size, color):
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y - size)      # start at the bottom so (x, y) is the middle
    t.pendown()
    t.color(color)
    t.begin_fill()
    t.circle(size)
    t.end_fill()


for i in range(30):
    x = 0          # TODO: random.randint(-350, 350)
    y = 0          # TODO: random.randint(-250, 250)
    size = 30      # TODO: random.randint(10, 50)
    color = PALETTE[4]    # TODO: random.choice(PALETTE)
    bubble(x, y, size, color)

turtle.done()
